title: Implement bounded probe window in scheduler to prevent probe amplification and define rollback criteria
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: After last week's capacity surge, we observed repeated short-lived kernel probe waves that amplified on high-concurrency workloads and caused ~15% p95 latency regression for certain attention-heavy workloads. Root cause analysis indicates the scheduler's probe window was unbounded under rapidly changing batch sizes, allowing repeated speculative kernel probes to re-enter the pipeline before previous probes settled. This ticket implements a bounded probe window (time + event budget) and a lightweight circuit-breaker to prevent amplification while preserving the scheduler's ability to discover better kernel candidates. Goals: (1) stabilize p95/p99 on mixed-attention workloads, (2) avoid adding steady-state latency, (3) provide clear rollback and canary criteria.
repro_steps: 1) Deploy a runbook cluster with runtime-1.21 + current scheduler branch. 2) Run synthetic workload generator 'seq-peak' configured with bursty arrivals (20k small requests/minute for 30s, then 5s idle) and mixed attention patterns (dense and sparse). 3) Observe scheduler logs for repeated kernel_probe events and correlate with batch eviction traces and KV cache misses. 4) Measure tail latency (p95/p99) and percent of requests that experienced kernel recompile or fallback within 500ms.
impact_summary: Observed impact: p95 latency regressions of ~15% and increased CPU/GPU context switches during probe amplification windows. Customer-facing effects limited to higher tail latency on sustained bursty arrival patterns — internal dashboards flagged the regression for a subset of PLG customers. No data exposure or incorrect responses were observed.
action_items: Design: specify probe window as two dimensions: maximum time window (W ms) and event budget (N probes) per worker per candidate-model, default W=250ms, N=3
Implement: throttle in scheduler that suppresses additional speculative probes once budget exhausted, with token-bucket style replenishment on steady state
Testing: add unit tests covering time-window expiry and budget replenishment; integrate an e2e synthetic test in CI that simulates bursty arrivals
Canary: rollout to 10% of runtime-dedicated pools with enhanced logging (probe_histogram) and compare p95 over 6-hour windows
Monitoring: add alerts for (a) probe suppression rate > 5% sustained, (b) p95 latency delta > 8% vs baseline for canary pools
Docs: update scheduler design doc and ops runbook with new knobs and recommended defaults
Follow-up: evaluate whether default W/N need adjustments for quantized kernels and multi-tenant noisy neighbors
rollout_plan: Phase A (dev): merge feature behind feature-flag 'bounded_probe_window' and run stress harness for 48h. Phase B (canary): enable for a subset of dedicated clusters (10%) for 72h; monitor p50/p95/p99 and probe suppression rate. Phase C (regional ramp): 50% for 48h, then global if metrics stable. Backstop: automatic disable of flag if rollback criteria tripped.
rollback_criteria: Canary p95 increases by >8% compared to canary baseline for 30m rolling window
Sustained increase in probe suppression >10% accompanied by p99 degradation
Unexpected increase in GPU utilization >12% without corresponding throughput gains
Any customer incident opened referencing scheduler-induced failures
monitoring_playbook: Metric: scheduler.kernel_probe.count (per-10s) - expected to decrease during bounded windows
Metric: scheduler.probe_suppressed.count (per-10s) - should be low in steady-state; alert if >5% of probes suppressed
Metric: runtime.latency.p95/p99 segmented by model and request-size - track delta vs baseline
Logging: retain probe_histogram traces for canary pools for 72h
Dashboards: add 'bounded-probe-window' overlay to existing scheduler-stability dashboard
Runbook steps: on alert, (1) scope to canary pools, (2) check recent PRs and flag state, (3) flip feature-flag to disable, (4) capture heap/profile and open postmortem if customer impact
